transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: 60m | Attendees: Tess Alvarez (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Quasar, Head of ML), Sara Morales (Quasar, Platform Eng), Kevin Liu (Quasar, CTO)

Summary: Quick scoping for POC timeline and milestones focused on benchmarks (latency, cost), workload sizing, access needs, and exec readout.

00:00:05 - Tess Alvarez: hey everyone thanks for joining, can we do quick intros?
00:00:12 - Daniel Park: yeah dan here, head of ml, we own recommendations and personalization at quasar
00:00:18 - Sara Morales: sara platform eng, i'll handle infra access
00:00:22 - Kevin Liu: kevin, cto, i'll mainly be involved for exec readout and high-level requirements
00:00:30 - Tess Alvarez: great. maya from our side?
00:00:34 - Maya Chen: hey all, maya se, i'll run the benchmarks and help with model integration and perf tuning

00:01:05 - Tess Alvarez: goal for today is agree success criteria, size the workload for the benchmark, and lock timeline for kickoff/midpoint/exec readout. any immediate constraints we should know?
00:01:20 - Daniel Park: our big constraint is latency on 99th percentile, currently at ~220ms serving 16k daily active users, we want to get that down but cost is also a big worry. we can't afford a 3x cost delta.
00:01:45 - Kevin Liu: and security: we need SOC2+ISO type evidence, plus data must not leave our VPC for the private option.
00:01:55 - Tess Alvarez: understood. for POC we typically offer two tracks: hosted to prove end-to-end quickly, and dedicated/private for perf/cost validation. which do you want to focus on?
00:02:10 - Daniel Park: i'd like dedicated+private routing, if possible — we want to validate our production-like environment. but we can start hosted if access delays happen.
00:02:25 - Maya Chen: ok, from the SE side we'll need a sample dataset, traffic profile (qps, seq len distribution), and a service account or vm with network peering or VPN. typical bench runs are steady-state + spike tests.

00:03:05 - Sara Morales: we can provide a 48-hour anonymized sample dataset and a traffic generator. on network we prefer VPC peering; VPN might be slower to provision.
00:03:20 - Maya Chen: VPC peering works — we'll need an IAM/service account that can pull model artifacts if we're doing private infra, or just API keys for hosted.

00:05:00 - Tess Alvarez: let's talk success criteria. typical things we track: latency p50/p90/p99, cost per 1M tokens, stability (error rate), and fidelity compared to your current model (we'll run evals on your test set). what thresholds are you thinking?
00:05:24 - Daniel Park: p99 under 200ms would be ideal, p90 under 80ms, and unit cost no more than 1.5x current spend. for fidelity we need top-k recall within 2% of our baseline.
00:05:45 - Kevin Liu: executive criteria will be: demonstrate consistent latency SLO, show predictable per-unit cost, and a plan for rollout to 50% of traffic.

00:07:10 - Maya Chen: sounds doable; we should capture workload sizing. can you confirm avg QPS and peak QPS for recommendations?
00:07:20 - Daniel Park: average 20 QPS, peak 100 QPS during promotions, average seq len ~128 tokens, 95th seq len 256. payload sizes small but cold-starts matter.
00:07:40 - Maya Chen: okay for POC we'll run tests at 25 QPS steady-state and a spike test to 110 QPS for 10 minutes to simulate promo. that'll validate autoscaling and batching.

00:08:30 - Tess Alvarez: benchmark plan: week 0 kickoff; week 1 access + infra setup; week 2 run baseline benchmarks (latency, throughput, cost); week 3 perf tuning and mid-point review; week 4-5 run extended regression and stability tests; week 6 exec readout. that maps to a 6-week POC.
00:08:55 - Sara Morales: are you expecting Redwood to spin up dedicated capacity or will we provision machines?
00:09:05 - Maya Chen: for Dedicated we'll provision reserved capacity on Redwood side but we need VPC peering and we may ask you to open a private peering connection to a subnet for model runtime. if we do private on your infra we can provide an on-prem package but that adds time for networking and certs.
00:09:30 - Daniel Park: ok prefer Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering. what's the typical time to get that fully provisioned?
00:09:38 - Tess Alvarez: typically 5-10 business days once networking and SSO are provisioned; if certs or HSM are needed it could take longer.

00:11:00 - Maya Chen: benchmarks we'll run: cold-start latency, steady-state latency at target QPS, p99 under load, token cost estimate using your traffic profile, and quality regression on the labeled eval set. we'll provide a harness and scripts.
00:11:15 - Daniel Park: good. how will you measure cost? we need a reproducible calculation we can plug into our finance model.
00:11:25 - Maya Chen: we'll provide a cost-per-token breakdown, plus a per-minute instance cost and guidance for batching settings that change unit economics. we'll share the raw measurement sheet you can drop into your model.

00:13:00 - Kevin Liu: security questions: SSO/SAML for console? KMS integration for keys? audit logs retention?
00:13:12 - Tess Alvarez: yes we support SAML SSO and RBAC, KMS integrations, and audit logs; we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts and a runbook. for the POC we can provide limited retention logs and then increase for ent.

00:15:00 - Daniel Park: timeline dependency: we have an exec review scheduled mid-december; is the 6-week POC too long for that?
00:15:12 - Tess Alvarez: if you need an earlier exec readout we can do a compressed 4-week pilot: kickoff/setup in week 1, baseline perf in week 2, quick tuning + mid-point in week 3, exec summary in week 4. tradeoff is less time for extended stability testing.
00:15:35 - Daniel Park: we might want the compressed path. let's tentatively plan for 4 weeks and keep 6-week as fallback.

00:16:10 - Maya Chen: technical note: for fidelity checks we'll need your ground truth labels and a sampling strategy; also any post-processing hooks you run in production (reranking, filters) so we can mirror behavior.
00:16:30 - Daniel Park: we'll share the eval set and a doc of post-processing steps.

00:18:00 - Tess Alvarez: ok action items — we'll capture and send over the harness, SOW, and security docs. who will be our main contact for infra access?
00:18:10 - Sara Morales: me, sara.m@quasar.com. i'll create a service account and open a peering request by Monday.
00:18:22 - Tess Alvarez: great. maya will send the harness link and instructions.
00:18:28 - Maya Chen: yes i'll post to the shared drive, link in the notes, includes load scripts and cost calc sheet.

00:20:00 - Kevin Liu: curious about fallback policies — if Dedicated capacity spikes beyond the reserved, what happens?
00:20:12 - Tess Alvarez: Redwood offers burst capacity and automatic fallback to compatible model variants in hosted zones; we'll document limits and costs. during POC we can simulate a burst and measure impact.

00:22:00 - Daniel Park: final questions on success criteria: confirm we have p99 <200ms, cost <1.5x, and fidelity within 2% — are those locked?
00:22:12 - Tess Alvarez: we'll record those as tentative success criteria and put them in the SOW: p99 target 200ms, cost target 1.5x current, and recall within 2%. if we cannot meet them we'll document blockers and next steps.

00:24:00 - Tess Alvarez: recap and milestones: Kickoff (11/26) - access & harness setup (week 1) - baseline runs (week 2) - mid-point review (week 3) - extended tests (week 4, optional week 5) - exec readout (week 4 compressed / week 6 full).
00:24:30 - Tess Alvarez: next steps we agreed: maya to share harness 11/21, tess to send SOW 11/22, quasar to provide sample dataset & access 11/24, kickoff 11/26 10am PT.

00:25:10 - Daniel Park: ok sounds good. thanks everyone. we'll aim for compressed 4-week path subject to access timelines.
00:25:20 - Tess Alvarez: thanks, we'll follow up in email with links and a calendar invite.

(Transcript ends, auto-generated sections: Topics: POC scope, success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, timeline. Action items present above. Some transcription noise: proper nouns occasionally mis-transcribed.)
